I have enough to write the explanation now.

## How the write side keeps the index in sync

When someone edits an issue title, the write goes through `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts:83-109`. After it authorizes the change (`assertOrgScope`, `assertCan(actor, "issue:update", ...)`, `assertNotArchived`) and persists it via `issueRepo.updateIssue(input)`, it calls `await emit("issue.updated", {...})` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts`. That `emit` is awaited and fans out synchronously (via `Promise.allSettled`) to every subscriber of `"issue.updated"`, so the caller of `updateIssue` doesn't return until indexing has been attempted.

The search indexer registers its interest in `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts:145-182`. Its `"issue.updated"` handler does **not** trust the event payload's title — it re-reads the row with `issueRepo.findIssueById(payload.orgId, payload.issueId)` and, if found, calls `indexIssue(orgId, issue)`. That deliberate re-read (noted in the comment above `registerSearchListeners`) means a partially-applied or since-superseded write can never get indexed as if it succeeded — the index always reflects the current row, not the event's snapshot.

`indexIssue` (`search-service.ts`) builds the document content as `[issue.title, issue.description ?? ""].join("\n")` and calls `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument(orgId, "issue", issue.id, content, issue.projectId)`. In `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`, `upsertSearchDocument` looks for an existing row keyed by `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)` — not by the search row's own id — and either updates `content`/`projectId`/`indexedAt` on that row or inserts a new one. Keying by the subject rather than the index row's id is what makes the indexer idempotent under repeated `issue.updated` events. The denormalized table is `searchIndex` (`src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`'s `SearchIndexRow`), storing `orgId`, `subjectKind`, `subjectId`, `projectId`, `content`, and `indexedAt` — just a flat text blob per subject, no separate tokenization.

There's also a fallback path: `subscribe("search.reindex_requested", ...)` re-indexes an issue on demand (driven by `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts`), used to repair drift rather than as the primary sync mechanism.

## How the colleague's query gets back results

The command palette hits `GET /api/search` (`src/app/api/search/route.ts`), while the search page uses the `searchAction` Server Action in `src/actions/search/search.ts` — both are described as deliberately duplicating the same gating so neither is more lenient.

In the route handler: it reads `orgSlug`/`q`, resolves `actor` via `getActor(orgSlug)`, then checks `can(actor, "org:read", ...)` — refusing with `403 forbidden` if the colleague isn't a member of that org. It loads the org summary and builds a flag context (`buildFlagContext`), then checks `isEnabled("command_palette", context)` — if the command palette isn't enabled for that org/plan, it's refused as well. It parses the query with `searchQuerySchema.safeParse`, scoping `kinds` to `["issue", "comment", "project"]` only if `advanced_search` is enabled (else just `["issue"]`); a schema failure returns `validation_failed`.

The parsed input then goes to `search()` in `search-service.ts`, which does its own authorization independent of the route: `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` and `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", ...)` — a hard throw, not a boolean check, since this is the shared core both entry points call into. Then `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` is checked against the token bucket in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` (capacity 120, refill 60/min, scaled by the org's plan via `getPlanLimits`); if exhausted, the query is refused with a "Search rate limit reached" error even though it's otherwise perfectly valid.

Next, `search()` re-checks `advanced_search` for the org's actual plan (not just the palette's cached context) and rejects with "Field-scoped search is not included in this plan" if `input.q` contains a `:` (field-scoped syntax like `status:done`) but the org's plan doesn't include `advanced_search` — this is the other circumstance where a well-formed query is refused, gated purely by plan/feature flag rather than by the query's validity.

If it clears all of that, `searchRepo.searchDocuments(input)` runs the actual query — a tenant-scoped (`orgPredicate`), `LIKE %q%` substring match over `searchIndex.content`, optionally filtered by `kinds`/`projectId`, ordered by `indexedAt`/`id` for keyset pagination. Results are mapped back into `SearchHit`s (title taken from the first line of `content`, a snippet computed by `snippetAround`, and an `href` built by `hrefFor`) and returned to the colleague — reflecting whatever `indexIssue` last wrote for that issue, which is why the renamed title shows up "moments later": as soon as the synchronous `issue.updated` handler chain from the edit has completed.
